How Algorithmia Built The Largest Marketplace For Algorithms In The World

Algorithmia is a service that enables the creation of applications through the use of community contributed machine learning models. And Algorithmia is looking to advance the development and accessibility of algorithmic intelligence. Plus Algorithmia is also known for building the largest marketplace for algorithms in the world. Currently, the service has over 60,000 developers tapping into a library of over 4,500 algorithms. Many of those algorithms revolve around machine learning.

Algorithmia

Algorithmia's AI Layer

Late last year, Algorithmia announced a new service that helps data scientists deploy machine learning models and host it in the Algorithmia cloud (Serverless AI Layer) or using on-premises architecture (Enterprise). Algorithmia offers these services in two forms. The first form is a Serverless AI Layer for setting up models in the cloud. There is an Enterprise AI Layer for setting up the model in any public or private cloud. And both of these forms support the ability to deploy code bases from GitHub, set up permissions and share it with an organization.

Algorithmia was founded in December 2013 and it has raised $13 million total in seed and Series A funding. Algorithmia co-founder and CEO Diego Oppenheimer told me that he grew up in Uruguay and moved to the U.S. to attend Carnegie Mellon University where he received a BS in Information Systems and an MS in Data Analytics before starting the company. Prior to launching Algorithmia, he was a program manager at Microsoft where he worked on several multibillion-dollar data products including Excel SQL Server, PowerPivot, PowerQuery and Power BI.

Oppenheimer came up with the idea for Algorithmia with CTO and co-founder Kenny Daniel. Daniel was working towards his Ph.D. when he realized the impact that artificial intelligence and machine learning was going to have in the world. “A big frustration came from how hard it was to go from academic work to something companies and developers across the globe could consume. In Excel as soon as 2012 we were thinking about how machine learning methods could help our users and started seeing the difficulty of integrating these methods into everyday software,” said Oppenheimer in the interview.

Algorithmia

Algorithmia Screenshot Recommended by Forbes

The solution to that problem was to create a marketplace where data scientists and machine learning engineers could build and monetize artificial intelligence and machine learning models. And the goal was to democratize access to the most advanced artificial intelligence available. “We see a day in the not so distant future in which algorithms will be able to piece together models from our marketplace without a human programmer and create entirely new software applications from the components in the Algorithmia marketplace,” added Oppenheimer.

One of the catalysts for the creation of the company is when Oppenheimer and Daniel started talking to academics and developers about how they were approaching machine learning at a time when nobody was really talking about it. Oppenheimer and Daniel started first talking about it publicly on Hacker News a few years ago and the feedback was immediate with over 800 developers signing up right away. “Once we had that confidence it was time to actually get the first version of the marketplace running which took Kenny and I coding around the clock about 5 months to get an alpha version running,” explained Oppenheimer.

After hundreds of developers signed up and it was determined that people were willing to pay, the Algorithmia team started looking for investors. Fortunately, the company was able to find local investors in Seattle that understood the space well. For example, Madrona Venture Group led the seed round of funding in August 2014 and Algorithmia was able to hire several engineers. And Algorithmia made its system language agnostic so that artificial intelligence and machine learning models can be written in R, Python, or Scala and can be easily deployed with an API on software stack.

One of the biggest achievements that Oppenheimer told me about Algorithmia is how the company helped the University of California, Berkeley computer vision labs launch a project that could turn black-and-white photos into color photos. This project was seen by millions of people, appeared on the Reddit homepage and was published by more than 200 publications around the world. And this work was used so widely to the point that the proceeds from running the project on Algorithmia’s system led to the purchase of new hardware for their lab.

A number of governmental organizations also use Algorithmia’s services. “I have never seen a more passionate group of people about their mission and work of protecting this country. We enable them to quickly deploy their machine learning and data science models into production which translates to keeping US citizens and military safe across the globe,” Oppenheimer pointed out.

Last year, Google launched a new fund for investing in artificial intelligence companies. And its first investment in that fund was in Algorithmia’s Series A round of funding. It’s worth mentioning that Algorithmia received numerous acquisition offers, but the founders of the company were more interested in building out the business. Google was not one of the companies that offered an acquisition, but the search giant understands that every company is going to need to build or buy an AI Layer. In fact, Google’s VP of Engineering in the Artificial Intelligence Anna Patterson said that she is impressed with Algorithmia's serverless microservice architecture as she has spent many years designing and deploying machine learning systems. “For us, it was a win-win, a huge vote of confidence from the number one machine learning company in the world and an opportunity to work with them side by side while remaining independent,” Oppenheimer revealed.
